text: You are going to investigate the reaction between aqueous sodium carbonate and two different
solutions of dilute hydrochloric acid, labelled A and B.
Read all of the instructions carefully before starting the experiments.
Instructions
You are going to do three experiments.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Heat the first portion of solid C gently and test any gas given off with damp universal indicator
paper.
Record your observations.

To the second portion of solid C, add about 10cm of distilled water. Place a stopper in the boiling
tube and shake the boiling tube to dissolve solid C and form solution C.
Divide solution C into three approximately equal portions in two test-tubes and one boiling tube.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
To the first portion of solution C in a test-tube, add about 1cm depth of dilute nitric acid followed
by a few drops of aqueous barium nitrate.
Record your observations.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
To the second portion of solution C in a test-tube, add about 1cm depth of dilute nitric acid
followed by a few drops of aqueous silver nitrate.
Record your observations.

parts.label: (i)
parts.text:
To the third portion of solution C in a boiling tube, add about 1cm depth of aqueous
sodium hydroxide.
Keep the product for use in (d)(ii).
Record your observations.

parts.label: (ii)
parts.text:
Warm the product from (d)(i) and test any gas given off.
Record your observations.

parts.label: (e)
parts.text:
Identify solid C.

Tests on solid D

parts.label: (f)
parts.text:
Carry out a flame test on solid D.
Record your observations.

parts.label: (g)
parts.text:
To the boiling tube containing solid D, add about 5cm depth of dilute nitric acid. Test any gas
given off.
Keep the solution formed for use in (h).
Record your observations.

parts.label: (h)
parts.text:
Transfer about 1cm depth of the solution formed in (g) to a test-tube.
To the solution in the test-tube, add aqueous sodium hydroxide gradually until there is no
further change.
Record your observations.

parts.label: (i)
parts.text: Identify three ions present in solid D.

text: You are provided with two solids: solid C and solid D.
Do the following tests on the solids, recording all of your observations at each stage.
Tests on solid C
Divide solid C into two approximately equal portions in two boiling tubes.
When excess dilute sulfuric acid is added to solid zinc, hydrogen gas and aqueous zinc sulfate are
made.

Plan an experiment to show that copper is a catalyst for this reaction. Your plan should include how
the results of the experiment will show that copper is a catalyst for this reaction.
You are provided with zinc powder, dilute sulfuric acid, copper powder and common laboratory
apparatus.
